trust_decision.summary: Whether a network client may drive a module's node_helper (and the server-side fetch it performs) is decided by config.ipWhitelist, enforced only by the Express middleware in js/ip_access_control.js:50-61, which never sees Socket.IO requests because socket.io attaches its own request listener to the same http.Server (js/server.js:41-51); the fix therefore adds a second ipWhitelist guard as an Engine.IO allowRequest hook.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the newsfeed Socket.IO notification as the SSRF vector, so an engineer looks first at the newsfeed node_helper's socketNotificationReceived dispatch, which reaches the server-side fetch(url) at defaultmodules/newsfeed/node_helper.js:28 (triggered from defaultmodules/newsfeed/newsfeed.js:495); the actual fix is in the core socket setup, two directories away.

fix_sites.entry_point: Express HTTP surface of the mirror: app.use(ipAccessControl(config.ipWhitelist)) at js/server.js:90 covering GET /, /config, /cors, /version, /env, /startup, /reload and all static dirs

Socket.IO Engine.IO handshake at /socket.io/ for every namespace: the default namespace / (js/main.js:620) and each module namespace /<moduleName> (js/socketclient.js:15, registered at js/node_helper.js:88)
fix_sites.module_kind: second implementation of the same whitelist check, written for the (req, callback) allowRequest contract

fix_sites.entry_point: server bootstrap: socketio(server, { allowRequest: socketIpAccessControl(config.ipWhitelist) }) at fix.diff:99

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: js/ip_access_control.js:41-61 (the only whitelist guard at the pinned commit); the fix has to add a parallel guard for the socket transport at fix.diff:62-79 because the express (req, res, next) contract cannot be reused by socket.io's (req, callback) allowRequest signature

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Socket.IO is attached to the same http.Server that serves the Express app (js/server.js:41-43), so a solver can argue the ipWhitelist middleware already covers it and the socket transport is 'just another route'; likewise the newsfeed helper's fetch is the module's own concern, not the transport's.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An empty ipWhitelist ([]) is documented to mean allow-all for every client; a socket guard that treats an empty or non-array whitelist as deny-all locks the whole mirror UI (browser socket handshake included) out, which is why the published fix keeps a separate allow-all branch for the socket path

O6_input_shapes: x-forwarded-for present as a comma-separated multi-hop string -> first entry, trimmed (fix.diff:25-28)
x-forwarded-for absent, empty or whitespace-only -> fall back to the direct peer address (fix.diff:25-26)
x-forwarded-for carrying a non-string value (repeated header) -> ignored by the typeof check (fix.diff:26)
direct peer loopback written as 127.0.0.1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1 or ::1 -> forwarded value trusted (fix.diff:22-24)
direct peer not loopback -> forwarded value deliberately ignored to prevent spoofing (fix.diff:24-31)
whitelist empty array or non-array -> allow all (fix.diff:64-68)
whitelist entries as single addresses or CIDR ranges, IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 (js/ip_access_control.js:14-29, unchanged by the fix)

O7_producer.where: js/utils.js:102 (loadConfig) merging the ipWhitelist default from js/defaults.js:13 into configObj.fullConf, which is handed to the Server (js/app.js:188, js/app.js:233) and read at js/server.js:44 and js/server.js:90

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second socket.io server or an extra namespace created with its own options object and no allowRequest
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the guard is a construction-time option, so any new socketio(...) call or a module-added realtime endpoint silently skips it while still riding the same http.Server

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A node_helper that mounts routes on its own express app instead of the shared one handed over by setExpressApp
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setExpressApp exists precisely to let module authors add HTTP routes; the whitelist only applies because of registration order relative to js/server.js:90, an ordering nothing enforces

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another proxy-style handler (image or media proxy) with its own URL validation but no IP check of its own
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the /cors proxy shows the project already ships server-side fetch endpoints, so a sibling proxy route is a natural next feature and would rely entirely on the single app.use line

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another control route that triggers io.emit (like /reload) under a different path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: control endpoints are added ad hoc next to the static routes and inherit protection only from the one ipAccessControl app.use call

O9_family: ssrf (CWE-918) via missing IP access control on a second transport (CWE-284)

O10_build.toolchain: npm; engines node >=22.21.1 <23 || >=24 (package.json:133-135); vitest 4 (package.json:128); eslint/prettier; playwright chromium only for tests/e2e (package.json:124, tests/e2e/helpers/global-setup.js:43)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/e2e/ipWhitelist_spec.js:3-35 covers only the HTTP path (403 for tests/configs/noIpWhiteList.js, 200 for tests/configs/empty_ipWhiteList.js) via `npm run test:e2e` (package.json:69); no unit test for js/ip_access_control.js exists at the pinned commit — tests/unit/functions/ip_access_control_spec.js is added by fix.diff:132-216

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an allowRequest (or io.use) that compares req.socket.remoteAddress directly against the whitelist, leaving the Express path on req.ip and treating an empty whitelist as deny-all.

out_of_scope_notes: js/server_functions.js:47-135 is a separate, already-hardened SSRF area (the /cors proxy, referencing GHSA-xhvw-r95j-xm4v); noted only, not pursued.

The published fix newly trusts X-Forwarded-For from loopback peers (fix.diff:24-29), which lets any local process on a multi-user host present a whitelisted address; that is a post-pinned-commit change, not assessed here.
